answers.summary: Right now nothing is pending in Sacramento. The 2025-26 session ended August 31, 2026, the governor's sign/veto deadline passed September 30, and every bill that didn't make it is dead. The next fights start when the 2027-28 Legislature convenes in December 2026, and the live action until then is the November 3 ballot.
answers.answer:
### Where things stand (October 27, 2026)
California runs two-year sessions. The **2025-26 session ended August 31, 2026**. Governor Newsom's last day to sign or veto was **September 30, 2026**, and he used it. CAA reports he signed SB 1365, the emergency rent-cap expansion, on that final day. So in a technical sense **no housing or landlord-tenant bill is "pending" today**. Anything that didn't reach his desk, including two-year bills like **AB 1157 (Kalra)**, is dead and would have to be reintroduced.

### What carries over in practice
- **New session:** The 2027-28 Legislature convenes in early December 2026 for its organizational session, and bill introductions follow. Expect the tenant-side ideas that died in 2026 to come back under new numbers: a lower AB 1482 cap, coverage of single-family homes and condos, and removing the 2030 sunset.
- **The ballot:** On November 3 voters decide **Prop 1** (an $11.25B housing bond), **Prop 43** (a two-thirds vote for citizen-initiated local special taxes), **Prop 45** (a CEQA fast track) and **Prop 37** (CalHFA middle-income home loans). See Q159.
- **Implementation:** Most 2026 enactments take effect **January 1, 2027**. SB 1296's pet-policy disclosure rule becomes operative **April 1, 2027**. See Q158.

### Watch list for 2027
1. An **AB 1482 sunset extension**. The law expires January 1, 2030, so 2027-29 is when an extension or rewrite gets negotiated.
2. Follow-ups to **SB 1365**, the price-gouging caps on long leases after an emergency declaration.
3. **Transfer-tax** reform after the Howard Jarvis initiative was withdrawn and replaced by Prop 43.

**So what:** For owners, today's risk is not a pending bill but the **January 1, 2027 compliance changes** and the **2027 bill-introduction wave**. Re-check leginfo.legislature.ca.gov in late February 2027, after the bill-introduction deadline.

answers.summary: The big landlord bill of 2026 is **SB 1365**, signed September 30. Starting January 1, 2027 it extends the 10% post-emergency price-gouging cap to rentals with leases longer than a year. Also new: a written pet-policy rule (SB 1296, operative April 1, 2027), disclosure of digitally altered listing photos (AB 2025), and a large pro-supply package (density bonus, ADUs, tentative maps, CEQA). Nearly all of it takes effect January 1, 2027.
answers.answer:
### Landlord-tenant bills signed in 2026
| Bill | What it does | Signed | Effective |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SB 1365** (Allen) | Extends Penal Code 396 (10% cap on increases after an emergency declaration) to rentals with initial leases over 1 year; adds defenses for pre-agreed increases and recent capital work | Sept 30 | Jan 1, 2027 |
| **SB 1296** | Landlords must keep a written pet policy, post it in ads and give it with applications; application fee refunds if the policy disqualifies | Sept 30 | Operative Apr 1, 2027 |
| **AB 2025** | Disclose digitally altered rental photos | Sept 27 | Jan 1, 2027 |
| **SB 1160** | Eviction data reported by ZIP code | Sept 27 | Jan 1, 2027 |
| **AB 1957** (Pacheco) | Foreclosure-sale bidding window limited to tenants and nonprofits | Sept 18 | Jan 1, 2027 |

CAA opposed SB 1365 and asked for a veto. Violations of PC 396 are misdemeanors with fines of up to $10,000.

### Supply-side package (signed Sept 29-30, mostly effective Jan 1, 2027)
- **AB 2433:** Density Bonus Law overhaul.
- **AB 1751:** Missing Middle Townhome Act. Ministerial approval for up to 150 units; bars demolishing rent-controlled or tenant-occupied housing.
- **SB 1169:** Tentative maps last 48 months instead of 24.
- **AB 1621:** No more than two plan-check rounds.
- **SB 958:** Height alone is not a significant CEQA impact for qualifying infill projects.
- **AB 956 / SB 1117:** Two detached ADUs per lot; ADU impact fees apply only above 750 sq ft.
- **AB 1732:** CEQA housing exemption extended to 2037.

### Affordable-housing items
- **AB 2270:** Farmworker housing gets credit in tax-credit scoring.
- **SB 1091:** A buy-and-rehab affordability program.
- **AB 750:** Funding for at-risk affordable developments.
- **SB 417:** Signed June 25; placed Prop 1 on the ballot.

### Vetoed
Newsom vetoed AB 2166 on Sept 18 (backstop financing for housing factories), plus AB 1165, AB 1997, AB 2012, AB 306, AB 2439 and SB 1238.

**So what:** In wildfire-prone Ventura County, emergency declarations happen often. After January 1, 2027, a **12-month or longer lease no longer escapes the 10% cap**, so build that into post-fire renewals.

answers.summary: No rent-control or transfer-tax measure is on any Ventura County ballot on November 3, 2026. The housing-relevant items are statewide: **Prop 1** ($11.25B housing bond), **Prop 43** (two-thirds vote for citizen-initiated local special taxes), **Prop 45** (CEQA fast track) and **Prop 37** (CalHFA home loans). Locally there's Oxnard's Measure E sales-tax extension, Simi Valley's hotel-tax hike and several bonds.
answers.answer:
### Statewide propositions that matter to multifamily
| Prop | What it does | Placed by | Why owners care |

| **1** | $11.25B bond: $10B GO for affordable housing plus $1.25B CalVet revenue bonds (SB 417) | Legislature | $5.1B for MHP, $750M Portfolio Reinvestment, $200M to buy and restrict unrestricted units, $450M farmworker housing. More nonprofit buyers and competing new supply. CAA supports it. |

| **37** | Up to $25B in CalHFA revenue bonds for second loans to middle-income buyers of new homes | Petition | Could pull some renters into ownership |

Also on the ballot: Prop 3 (makes high-income tax rates permanent), Prop 40 (one-time billionaire tax, which excludes real estate), Props 41-42 (tax audits; ban on new personal-property taxes) and Prop 2 (reserves). **No statewide rent control, Costa-Hawkins or split-roll measure is on the ballot.**

answers.summary: Voters have rejected Costa-Hawkins repeal three times, each time with about 59-62% voting no: Prop 10 (2018), Prop 21 (2020) and Prop 33 (2024). There is no rent-control initiative on the 2026 ballot. Prop 34 (2024) limits the main funder's spending, so a 2028 attempt is possible but harder to bankroll.
answers.answer:
### The track record
| Measure | Year | What it would have done | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Prop 10** | 2018 | Repeal Costa-Hawkins; let cities regulate any rental, including post-1995 buildings and SFRs, and impose vacancy control | Failed, about 59% no |
| **Prop 21** | 2020 | Narrower: let cities regulate housing first occupied more than 15 years ago, with an exemption for small SFR owners | Failed, about 60% no |
| **Prop 33** | 2024 | Repeal Costa-Hawkins outright ("Justice for Renters Act") | Failed, 60.0% no (certified) |

The AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) bankrolled all three. CAA, CAR and allied groups funded the opposition.

### Why another initiative is harder
- **Prop 34 (2024) passed** at the same election. It restricts how certain health-care providers that rely on federal drug-discount revenue (in practice, AHF) can spend that money. That squeezes the main funding source. AHF has called Prop 34 unconstitutional, and the legal challenge is unresolved.
- **Nothing on the November 2026 ballot.** None of the 14 statewide propositions is a rent-control measure.
- The **legislative route also failed**. AB 1157, which would have tightened AB 1482's cap, died in Assembly Judiciary on January 13, 2026. Opponents cited Prop 33's 62% "no" margin.

### Prospects
Tenant groups said after 2024 that they would keep going. The realistic paths are:
1. A **2028 initiative**, harder to fund under Prop 34.
2. A **legislative push tied to AB 1482's 2030 sunset**.
3. **City-by-city ordinances** within Costa-Hawkins limits, as Oxnard and Ojai have done and Santa Barbara is doing.

**So what:** For underwriting, vacancy decontrol and the exemptions for post-1995 buildings and SFRs remain the base case through at least 2028. The real local risk is a city ordinance, not a statewide repeal.
keyPoints: Prop 10 (2018), Prop 21 (2020), Prop 33 (2024) all failed, each with about 59-62% no
Prop 33 certified result: 40.0% yes / 60.0% no
AHF funded all three; Prop 34 (2024) restricts its spending
No rent-control measure among the 14 props on the Nov 2026 ballot
Next realistic window: a 2028 initiative or the AB 1482 sunset fight before 2030

answers.summary: No bill to repeal or amend Costa-Hawkins advanced in the 2025-26 session; I found no such bill introduced. The last serious legislative try, SB 466 (Wahab), died February 1, 2024. The 2025-26 rent fight targeted AB 1482 (AB 1157), not Costa-Hawkins, and it also died.
answers.answer:
### What Costa-Hawkins does (1995)
- **New buildings:** Exempts housing first occupied after February 1, 1995 from local rent control.
- **Single-family homes and condos:** Exempts separately alienable single-family homes and condos.
- **Vacancy decontrol:** Guarantees it. When a tenant leaves a rent-controlled unit, the owner resets to market.

Those three features are why Oxnard's and Ojai's 4% caps only reach older apartment buildings.

### Recent legislative attempts
| Bill | Session | Idea | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| AB 1506 (Bloom) | 2019 | Full repeal | Failed in Assembly Housing Committee |
| **SB 466 (Wahab)** | 2023-24 | Rolling exemption, first 15 years, later amended; keep the SFR/condo exemption | Failed on the Senate floor (15-16) and died February 1, 2024 under Joint Rule 56 |
| AB 1157 (Kalra) | 2025-26 | Lower the **AB 1482** cap and extend it to SFRs and condos (not Costa-Hawkins) | Died in Assembly Judiciary January 13, 2026 (4 aye, 3 no, 5 abstain; needed 7) |

I found **no 2025-26 bill amending Costa-Hawkins**. The ballot route also failed three times (see Q160). With the session over, nothing is pending.

### What to expect
The idea most likely to return is a **rolling new-construction exemption**, for example 15 or 20 years, like Prop 21 and the original SB 466. A full repeal is less likely. Developers and CAA oppose rolling dates because they put future rent control on today's new construction. The Legislature has repeatedly declined to move these bills, and several Democrats abstained on AB 1157.

**So what:** For a buyer of a post-1995 Ventura County building, the exemption from local rent control is intact for now. AB 1482 (5% + CPI, max 10%) still applies unless the owner qualifies for its 15-year new-construction exemption. Price **some tail risk** that a rolling-exemption bill passes before you exit.
keyPoints: Costa-Hawkins: post-Feb 1, 1995 buildings and SFRs/condos exempt; vacancy decontrol
SB 466 (2023-24) died Feb 1, 2024 after failing 15-16 on the Senate floor
No Costa-Hawkins bill found in the 2025-26 session
AB 1157 (2025-26) targeted AB 1482, not Costa-Hawkins, and died Jan 13, 2026
Most likely future proposal: a rolling (e.g., 15-year) new-construction exemption

answers.summary: The main 2025-26 attempt was AB 1157 (Kalra). It would have cut AB 1482's cap to 2% + CPI (max 5%), covered single-family homes and condos, and deleted the 2030 sunset. It died in Assembly Judiciary on January 13, 2026. AB 1482 is unchanged at 5% + CPI (max 10%) and expires January 1, 2030 unless extended.
answers.answer:
### AB 1482 today (Civil Code 1947.12 / 1946.2)
- **Cap:** 5% plus regional CPI, maximum **10%** in any 12 months.
- **Just cause:** Required after 12 months of tenancy.
- **Key exemptions:**
  - Buildings issued a certificate of occupancy within the past **15 years** (rolling).
  - SFRs and condos owned by individuals, with the required lease notice.
  - Deed-restricted affordable units.
  - An owner-occupied duplex.
- **Sunset:** **January 1, 2030.** The statute requires an LAO report on the law's effects by then.
- SB 567 (2023) tightened the no-fault just-cause rules starting April 1, 2024.

### The 2025-26 attempt: AB 1157
| Proposal | Current law | AB 1157 |
|---|---|---|
| Cap | 5% + CPI, max 10% | 2% + CPI, max 5% |
| SFRs, condos, ADUs | Exempt (with notice) | Covered |
| Sunset | Jan 1, 2030 | Removed (permanent) |

Outcome: AB 1157 cleared Assembly Housing in 2025 but stalled in Judiciary. On **January 13, 2026** it got **4 ayes, 3 noes and 5 abstentions** when it needed 7, and it died. CAA and CAR opposed it, and ACCE and PICO rallied for it.

I found no other 2025-26 bill that changed AB 1482's cap, sunset or exemptions. A separate bill, **SB 1365**, extends the emergency **price-gouging** cap (PC 396) to leases over a year starting January 1, 2027 (see Q158). It is not an AB 1482 amendment.

### What's next
The **2030 sunset forces the issue**. Expect an extension bill in 2027-29, likely paired with tenant-side asks: a lower cap, SFR coverage and permanence. Industry will push for a straight extension.

**So what:** Underwrite 5% + CPI (max 10%) on covered units through 2029. Sensitivity-test a 2%-5% cap scenario after 2030. Track when the **15-year exemption expires** on newer Ventura County buildings you sell or buy.
keyPoints: AB 1482: 5% + CPI, max 10%; just cause after 12 months; sunsets Jan 1, 2030
Rolling exemption for buildings with a certificate of occupancy in the last 15 years
AB 1157 sought 2% + CPI (max 5%), SFR/condo coverage and no sunset
AB 1157 died Jan 13, 2026 in Asm. Judiciary: 4 aye, 3 no, 5 abstain (needed 7)
Expect an extension fight in 2027-29 ahead of the 2030 sunset

answers.summary: The active fronts are Oxnard, which is building out its 2022 4% rent cap (fair-return rules in February 2026, a new program-fee study in mid-2026), and the City of Ventura, which rejected rent stabilization in May 2025 but adopted an anti-harassment ordinance in early 2026. Ojai has had a 4% cap since 2023. Elsewhere the action is on mobile-home space rents (Santa Paula forums in 2026).
answers.answer:
### City by city (as of October 2026)
| Jurisdiction | Apartments | 2025-26 activity |
|---|---|---|
| **Oxnard** | 4% cap on pre-Feb 1995 buildings; just cause (adopted April 2022) | Fair-return petition rules adopted Feb 2026. Draft fee study (June 2026, proposed $70/$140 per unit, not yet adopted) with community meetings in summer 2026 |
| **Ojai** | 4% cap, Ord. 937 (2023) | In force |
| **City of Ventura** | No rent cap | Council rejected rent stabilization, a registry, TOPA and deposit limits on May 27, 2025. Kept working on anti-harassment, relocation and legal aid; anti-harassment ordinance adopted Feb 2026 |
| **Santa Paula** | None | 2026 community forums on a *mobile home* rent ordinance |
| **Unincorporated county** | None | Mobile home park rent control only (2.8% allowed for 2026) |
| Thousand Oaks, Camarillo, Simi Valley, Moorpark, Fillmore, Port Hueneme | None found beyond legacy or mobile-home programs | No active apartment study found |

### Who is pushing
Tenant groups (CAUSE, based in Ventura and active in Oxnard, Ventura and Santa Paula) push "Housing for All" protections. Apartment associations (CAA, AAGLA) track and fight each step.

### Read-across from Santa Barbara
Santa Barbara adopted a stricter ordinance in late September 2026 (see Section 10). Ventura County councils will hear it cited as a model in 2027.

**So what:**
- **Oxnard and Ojai:** The 4% cap and registry/fee costs are real underwriting inputs.
- **City of Ventura:** Rent stabilization was voted down in 2025, but the council keeps adding tenant rules. Expect it to resurface after council turnover. Four council seats were on the November 2026 ballot.
- **Everywhere else:** AB 1482 is the ceiling for now.

answers.summary: No. I found no ULA-style transfer tax proposed or on the ballot in any Ventura County city. Sellers pay the standard county documentary transfer tax of $1.10 per $1,000. If Prop 43 passes, any future citizen-initiative transfer tax would need a two-thirds vote starting in 2027.
answers.answer:
### Current state
- **County documentary transfer tax:** $1.10 per $1,000 of value (0.11%), the standard California county rate.
- **City transfer taxes:** Only charter cities can levy one above the county rate. I found none in Ventura County comparable to LA's Measure ULA, which charges 4% above about $5.4M and 5.5% above about $10.9M for closings after June 30, 2026.
- **November 3, 2026 ballot:** No local transfer-tax measure. The Ventura County measures are a hotel tax (Simi Valley A), a sales-tax extension (Oxnard E), and school and water bonds.

### Statewide backdrop that limits future attempts
1. **The Howard Jarvis initiative was withdrawn** in June 2026. It would have capped transfer taxes at 0.11% statewide and voided some taxes passed by majority vote, such as ULA.
2. In exchange, the Legislature put **Prop 43 (ACA 22)** on the ballot. It requires a **two-thirds vote for citizen-initiated local special taxes** starting January 1, 2027, and it leaves existing taxes, ULA included, in place. ULA itself passed by citizen initiative with a simple majority.
3. In LA, the council in June 2026 directed drafting of a possible ULA exemption for new multifamily. Reform there remains unsettled.

### Revenue pressure is real, though
The City of Ventura considered a 1% sales tax (about $36M a year) and voted 4-3 on June 2, 2026 not to place it on the ballot. One councilmember said it could return in 2028 or 2030. Cities looking for revenue will look at sales, hotel and parcel taxes first.

**So what:** For Ventura County dispositions, budget roughly 0.11% county transfer tax, plus any city tax only after checking the specific city's code. The ULA-style risk is low near term. A council-placed (not citizen-initiated) general tax would still need only a majority even if Prop 43 passes.

answers.summary: No split-roll or Prop 13 reassessment measure is on the 2026 ballot or advanced in the Legislature. The last split-roll attempt, Prop 15 in 2020, narrowly failed. The 2026 tax measures cut the other way: Prop 43 (two-thirds for citizen-initiated special taxes) and Prop 42 (no new personal-property taxes). Only small, targeted property-tax tweaks passed in 2026.
answers.answer:
### Prop 13 basics for multifamily
- **Rate and assessment:** 1% base rate plus voter-approved debt, roughly 1.1% in much of Ventura County. Assessed value resets to purchase price at a change in ownership, then rises no more than 2% a year.
- **Entity transfers:** Matter. A more-than-50% change in control of a legal entity triggers reassessment (R&T Code 64).

### Split roll: where it stands
| Effort | Year | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Prop 15 ("Schools and Communities First," commercial and industrial split roll; residential, including apartments, excluded) | 2020 | Failed narrowly |
| Any 2025-26 split-roll bill or ACA | 2025-26 | None advanced, as far as I could find |
| Nov 2026 ballot | 2026 | No split-roll or Prop 13 measure among the 14 props |

Even Prop 15 **excluded residential property, including apartments**. A future split roll would most likely target commercial and industrial property first.

### What did move in 2026
- **Prop 43 (on the ballot):** Two-thirds vote for citizen-initiated local special taxes, including parcel taxes.
- **Prop 42 (on the ballot):** Bars new state taxes on personal property such as financial assets. It does not cover real estate.
- **Prop 40 (on the ballot):** One-time 5% billionaire tax. Real estate is excluded from its base.
- **AB 1294 (reported signed Sept 29, 2026):** A pilot partial welfare exemption for qualifying nonprofit-owned middle-income rentals (up to 120% AMI) in Alameda County, Sacramento County and San Francisco only, for lien dates 2027-2029.
- **SB 296:** A partial exemption for disabled veterans' homes.

**So what:** Prop 13 protection for apartments is stable. Buyers still face full reassessment at purchase, and that drives the classic "low-basis long-term owner" seller profile in Ventura County. Watch for a 2028 split-roll initiative. Labor and education coalitions have tried before.
keyPoints: No split-roll or Prop 13 measure on the Nov 2026 ballot
Prop 15 (2020) split roll failed narrowly and excluded residential, including apartments
Prop 13: 1% base plus bonds; 2%/yr assessment cap; reset on change in ownership
Prop 43 and Prop 42 on the 2026 ballot tighten tax limits rather than loosen them
AB 1294 welfare-exemption pilot covers only Alameda, Sacramento and SF

answers.summary: The 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21, signed July 4, 2025) made **100% bonus depreciation permanent** for property acquired after January 19, 2025, **expanded LIHTC** (a permanent 12% boost to 9% credits and a lower bond test), and **left 1031 alone**. For agency debt, FHFA set 2026 caps at $88B each for Fannie and Freddie. Further LIHTC expansion (AHCIA) has no clear path in 2026.
answers.answer:
### Already law (One Big Beautiful Bill Act, P.L. 119-21)
| Item | Change | Multifamily angle |
|---|---|---|
| **Bonus depreciation** | Permanent **100%** for qualified property acquired after January 19, 2025 | Cost segregation on acquisitions front-loads write-offs from the 5-, 7- and 15-year components |
| **Section 179** | Limit raised to $2.5M (phase-out at $4M) | Useful for smaller owners' equipment and improvements |
| **LIHTC (9%)** | Permanent **12%** increase in state allocations from 2026 | California's 2026 ceiling uses **$3.416 per capita** (Rev. Proc. 2025-32) |
| **LIHTC (4%)** | The 50% tax-exempt bond test is permanently lowered (to 25% for bonds issued after 2025) | Stretches California's scarce bond cap to more 4% deals |
| **Opportunity Zones** | Program extended; rural QOZ substantial-improvement test cut to 50% | New designation rounds |
| **Section 1031** | **No change** | Like-kind exchanges of real property remain intact |

### Proposed or pending
- **AHCIA** (the rest of the LIHTC wish list): The ACTION Campaign says there is "no clear path" for tax legislation in 2026; a lame-duck deal is possible.
- **Other introduced bills, no action:** FIXER Act (H.R. 9906, preservation bonds outside the volume cap) and S. 5553 (a 30% bigger bond cap and transit basis boosts).
- **ROAD to Housing Act:** Contains LIHTC-related provisions; final status unconfirmed.

### Agency lending
FHFA's **2026 caps are $88B each** for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac ($176B total), released November 24, 2025. At least **50%** must be mission-driven affordable, and workforce-housing loans are excluded from the cap. FHFA said it would not lower the caps mid-year.

**So what:**
- **Sellers:** 1031 is safe, so the exchange-buyer pool stays intact.
- **Buyers:** 100% bonus depreciation improves after-tax returns on value-add deals.
- **Affordable developers:** More 9% and 4% capacity means more LIHTC competition for sites and acquisitions in Ventura County.
keyPoints: P.L. 119-21 enacted July 4, 2025
100% bonus depreciation made permanent for property acquired after Jan 19, 2025
LIHTC: permanent 12% boost to 9% credits; 2026 CA ceiling based on $3.416 per capita
1031 like-kind exchanges unchanged
FHFA 2026 caps: $88B each for Fannie and Freddie; 50% mission-driven

answers.summary: The owner side is led by the **California Apartment Association**, CAR and its local REALTOR boards, plus AAGLA and Howard Jarvis on taxes. They fought AB 1157 and SB 1365 and back Props 1 and 43. The tenant side is led locally by **CAUSE** (Ventura and Oxnard), with ACCE, PICO and Tenants Together statewide. Their focus is AB 1482 expansion, local rent caps and anti-harassment rules.
answers.answer:
### Owner and industry side
| Group | 2025-26 positions on record |
|---|---|
| **California Apartment Association (CAA)** | Opposed AB 1157 (it died Jan 2026). Opposed SB 1365 and asked for a veto (signed anyway). **Supports Prop 1**. Tracks Oxnard's RSO closely. |
| **California Association of REALTORS (CAR)** and local boards | Opposed AB 1157. Local boards weigh in on city ordinances. |
| **AAGLA** | Reports on and lobbies Ventura County councils, e.g., the May 2025 rejection of rent stabilization in Ventura. |
| **Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Assn.** | Withdrew its transfer-tax-cap initiative for Prop 43. Recommends YES on 41, 42, 43, 45 and NO on Props 1-5, 37, 38, 40, 44. |
| **CalChamber** | Sponsor of Prop 45 (CEQA fast track). |

### Tenant side
| Group | Focus |
|---|---|
| **CAUSE** (Central Coast Alliance United for a Sustainable Economy; Ventura office, active in Oxnard, Ventura and Santa Paula) | "Housing for All" campaigns, tenant know-your-rights, and support for local protections |
| **ACCE** and **PICO** | Rallied at the Capitol for AB 1157 the day before its January 2026 vote |
| **Tenants Together** | Statewide tenant network; tracks local rent ordinances |
| **AIDS Healthcare Foundation** | Funded Props 10, 21 and 33; constrained by Prop 34 |
| **Courage California** | Progressive voter guide; flagged CAA PAC money to AD 38 incumbent Steve Bennett as "problematic" |

### What each side is pushing in 2027
- **Tenant side:**
  - Revive AB 1157-type limits: a lower cap, SFR coverage and no sunset.
  - More local caps or registries (Ventura City after council turnover).
  - Relocation payments.
  - Anti-harassment rules.
- **Owner side:**
  - A clean AB 1482 extension, or a lapse.
  - Pass Prop 1 and Prop 43.
  - Fair-return protections in Oxnard and Ojai.
  - Resist post-emergency rent rules.

**So what:** Join CAA's alerts and your local REALTOR board's government-affairs list. Local ordinance fights are won or lost in 2-3 council meetings with little notice.

CAR also opposed AB 1157; HJTA backs Props 41, 42, 43, 45
CAUSE (Ventura-based) is the main local tenant organizer: Oxnard, Ventura, Santa Paula
ACCE and PICO rallied for AB 1157 in January 2026

Other nearby members whose lines may clip the county edges: AD 37 Gregg Hart (D, Santa Barbara), AD 40 Pilar Schiavo (D), AD 44 Nick Schultz (D), SD 23 Suzette Martinez Valladares (R). Confirm exact city splits before relying on them.

### Housing record (public actions only)
- **Limón:** Co-lead with Speaker Rivas on **SB 417**, the Prop 1 bond (signed June 25, 2026). She spoke at the bond rollout. As Pro Tem she controls which bills reach the Senate floor.
- **Bennett:** Courage California's guide flags a CAA PAC contribution to his campaign. That is a funding fact, not a vote.
- **Irwin:** Leaving the Assembly. She was first elected in 2014, which reaches the 12-year limit; she is not on the 2026 ballot.
- **Stern:** His office reports all nine of his 2026 bills were signed. I found no major landlord-tenant bill among them.
- **AB 1157:** None of these members sat on Assembly Judiciary for the January 2026 vote, so there is no recorded AB 1157 committee vote from them.

**So what:** For a client in Oxnard or Ventura, the Bennett and Limón offices matter. For Thousand Oaks and Simi Valley, Stern and the AD 42 winner matter. Limón's Pro Tem role makes SD 21 unusually influential on any 2027 rent bill.

answers.summary: The five supervisors are believed to be Matt LaVere (D1), Jeff Gorell (D2), Kelly Long (D3), Janice Parvin (D4) and Vianey Lopez (D5), but I could not confirm the roster or recent housing votes from an official source this session. The county's direct rental role is narrow: unincorporated areas have no apartment rent control, only a 1983 mobile home park program (2.8% cap for 2026).
answers.answer:
### Roster (needs confirmation)
| District | Supervisor (as of last confirmed) | General area |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Matt LaVere | City of Ventura, Ojai Valley, west county |
| 2 | Jeff Gorell | Thousand Oaks, Conejo Valley, part of Camarillo, coast |
| 3 | Kelly Long | Camarillo, Santa Paula, Fillmore, Piru, part of Oxnard plain |
| 4 | Janice Parvin | Simi Valley, Moorpark |
| 5 | Vianey Lopez | Oxnard, Port Hueneme, El Rio |

Districts 2 and 4 were on the 2026 cycle. I could not confirm whether they were decided in the June primary. **Verify the current roster, 2026 chair and district lines before quoting.**

### Where the Board actually touches multifamily
- **Unincorporated rentals:** No apartment rent control or local just-cause ordinance. AB 1482 applies.
- **Mobile home parks:** A 1983 rent control ordinance covers about 1,390 spaces in 25 parks. The 2026 ministerial increase is **2.8%**, overseen by a five-member Rent Review Board.
- **Growth limits:** SOAR (Save Open Space and Agricultural Resources) requires voter approval to rezone agricultural or open-space land in the unincorporated county. It was extended by voters to 2050. That pushes most multifamily into the cities.
- **Funding and partners:** The County partners with the Area Housing Authority, the Housing Trust Fund Ventura County and the Homekey projects (see Section 15). Farmworker housing in the unincorporated area (e.g., Somis Ranch) runs through county land-use approvals.

### Voting record
I did not find a reliable, sourced summary of individual supervisors' 2025-26 housing votes, such as housing element rezoning, farmworker housing ordinances or inclusionary rules. Rather than characterize anyone, pull the minutes.

**So what:** For apartment investors, the Board matters mostly for **unincorporated land use**, **farmworker and affordable financing** and **mobile home parks**. City councils set rent rules for the vast majority of the county's apartments.

SOAR requires a public vote to convert ag/open space (extended to 2050)
City councils, not the Board, set rent rules for most apartments
